draft.title: Force and levers
card: A force is a push or a pull. Muscles can only pull, and they pull on bones to move them.
A lever is a rigid bar that turns around a fixed point called the fulcrum. In the body, a bone is the lever and a joint is the fulcrum.
The muscle's pull is the effort. The weight of the body part, or of an object it holds, is the load. Effort acting on the lever moves the load.
Speed at release or contact depends on how much force is applied and for how long or how far. Applying force over a longer time or distance gives more speed.
draft.remember: Muscles pull on bones, which turn at joints. More force over more time or distance gives more speed.

a.q: In the body, which part acts as the fulcrum when a bone is moved by a muscle?
opts: The joint the bone turns around
The muscle that pulls on the bone
The bone that is being moved
The object held in the hand
a.why: A fulcrum is the fixed point a lever turns around, and in the body that is the joint. The bone is the lever, not the fulcrum, even though it is the part that moves.
a.clue: Which part stays fixed while the bone turns?

b.q: Two cricket bowlers are equally strong. Ravi swings his arm through a long arc before release. Tom swings through a short arc. Whose ball is likely to leave the hand faster, and why?
opts: Ravi's, because force acts over a longer distance
Tom's, because force acts over a shorter distance
Ravi's, because a longer arc makes his muscles push
Tom's, because a shorter arc needs less effort overall
b.why: With the same force, a longer arc means the force acts over a greater distance, which gives more speed at release. Tom's shorter arc gives the force less distance to act, so a shorter arc does not help.
b.clue: Both apply the same force, so look at the distance it acts over.

a.best: The joint the bone turns around

b.best: Ravi's, because force acts over a longer distance
